cards.text: Paul is writing to all the believers in Philippi (Philippians 1:1), and he's just told them to stand firm in the Lord (Philippians 4:1). Now, in a letter to the WHOLE church, he names two women: Euodia and Syntyche. Friend, that's your boss reading your name out loud at the staff meeting, and you just KNOW it's not for employee of the month.

cards.question: Paul names Euodia and Syntyche in his letter. What does he urge them to do?

answers.text: Agree with each other in the Lord
Come and visit him right away
Choose new leaders for the church

cards.text: Then Paul turns to someone he calls 'my true yokefellow,' with no name attached. If somebody called ME that, I'd be proud and confused at the same time.

cards.question: Paul asks his true yokefellow to help Euodia and Syntyche.
Paul tells his yokefellow what Euodia and Syntyche have done alongside him. What is it?

answers.text: Contended at his side for the gospel
Traveled with him all the way to Corinth
Hosted the whole church in their homes

cards.question: Paul also mentions Clement and the rest of his fellow workers. He says their names are in the Book of ___.

cards.text: Then Paul gets LOUD about one word, and right after saying it, he adds, 'I will say it again: Rejoice!' That's me telling a new baker the oven is HOT: once is information, twice means it REALLY matters.

cards.question: Paul tells the believers in Philippi to rejoice in the Lord only when things are going well.

cards.text: Next, Paul names something he wants everybody to be able to see in them, front and center like the best batch in my Display Case.

cards.question: Paul wants the believers' ___ to be apparent to all.

cards.text: Then Paul drops four short words: 'The Lord is near.' Right after that, he goes after worry, and friend, I spent YEARS in a junk drawer jumping every time it rattled, so I am LISTENING.

cards.question: Paul tells the believers in Philippi that some things are worth being anxious about.
Paul says to be anxious for nothing. Instead, in everything, what does he tell them to do with their requests?

answers.text: Present them to God with thanksgiving
Leave them unspoken and trust God
Present them to the elders with fasting

cards.text: Then Paul brings in the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding. Friend, most things surpass MY understanding, but this one does it on purpose.

cards.question: Paul says the peace of God will do something to their hearts and minds in Christ Jesus. What?

cards.text: Then Paul says 'Finally' and hands them a list: whatever is true, honorable, right, pure, lovely or admirable, and anything excellent or praiseworthy. That's a GOOD list, and my to-do list is one line that says 'stamp.'

cards.question: Paul lists whatever is true, honorable, right, pure, lovely and admirable. What does he tell them to do with these things?

cards.text: Last one: Paul points to himself, to whatever they learned or received or heard from him, or saw in him. Bold move, because if you watched ME work, you'd mostly learn how to get dough on the ceiling.

cards.question: Paul points to whatever they learned, received or heard from him, or saw in him. What does he tell them to do with it?
Paul ends with a promise: the God of ___ will be with them.

findings.problem: Paul appears here for the first time, but the card never says who he is. It only says he is writing to the believers in Philippi. It should briefly identify him, for example as Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, with its reference.

rule.text: **New people.** The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The right answer, 'Contended at his side for the gospel', uses the BSB's wording ('contended', 'for the gospel') and sounds more like the Bible than the two modern-sounding wrong answers, so it stands out. The question's word 'alongside him' also rules out 'Hosted the whole church in their homes', which isn't something done alongside Paul.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: Multiple choice is 6 of the 12 choice cards, while true or false and fill in the blank have 3 each. Cards 15, 17 and 19 are three multiple choice cards in a row at the end. Cards 17 and 19 also use the same question form ('What does he tell them to do with...'), which reads as a pattern.

rule.text: **No formula.** Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.
